refnamediv.refpurpose: Sign system reports with a set of signed TPM2 attestations

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-report-sign-tpm2@.service is a system service that signs system reports generated by systemd-report1. It is a signing backend for the --sign= logic of that tool: it implements the io.systemd.Report.Signer.Sign() Varlink method and is reached via a socket linked into the /run/systemd/report.sign/ directory, named tpm2.

The service is socket-activated (one instance per connection) via systemd-report-sign-tpm2.socket. Rather than returning a single signature, it uses a TPM2 device to generate a set of signed attestations that also bind the report digest passed to it, together providing a verifier with evidence about the state of the system that produced the report.

The returned report consists of several signed components, each carrying a JSON encoded attestation structure and its corresponding signature. The signature is provided as a JSON encoded TPMT_SIGNATURE structure and in PEM encoded form. The signed component types are:

listitem.para: A PCR quote, generated with TPM2_Quote

One attestation per NvPCR, generated with TPM2_NV_Certify. Each component also includes the readable name of the NvPCR, the NV index public area (as a JSON encoded TPMS_NV_PUBLIC structure), and a JSON blob of authenticated data (the NvPCR name and priority) that is digested and supplied as the qualifying data to the certify command.
An audit session attestation, generated with TPM2_GetSessionAuditDigest. This is always the last component. The report digest passed in via Varlink is supplied as its qualifying data.

refsect1.para: The report additionally includes the measurement event log, and the public area of the signing key. The public area is provided as a JSON encoded TPMT_PUBLIC structure, and in PEM encoded form.

The preceding components are all executed under the audit session, and the report is only generated if that session remains exclusive throughout. Because the audit session attestation records whether the session was still exclusive when it was signed, this provides evidence to a verifier that the report is a single, consistent snapshot of the system, with no other TPM commands interleaved while it was generated.

The set of attested PCRs and NvPCRs is currently fixed. It covers all firmware PCRs except PCR 6, all other S-RTM PCRs except the IMA PCR (which is not useful without the IMA log), and all defined NvPCRs.

refsect1.title: Signing keys
refsect1.para: The attestation signing keys are stored as JSON files named keyname.key in /var/lib/systemd/report.sign.tpm2/. Three kinds of key are supported: an ordinary object protected by an existing persistent object such as the SRK or EK, a persistent object (which may be created as an ordinary or primary object), and a primary object that is recreated from a template on each use. In all cases the keys must be restricted signing keys. If no keys exist, an ordinary key is generated automatically on first use and saved as default.key.

For ordinary and primary keys, the loaded object context is cached in the service's runtime directory as /run/systemd/report.sign.tpm2/keyname.context and reused on subsequent invocations, avoiding a repeated TPM2_Load (which requires authorization with the parent key), or a repeated TPM2_CreatePrimary (which requires authorization with the hierarchy and can be slow).

The key may optionally have an associated voucher, stored alongside it as keyname.voucher. This is an opaque credential — for example one issued by a CA during onboarding — that is attached to the signed report and presented to a verifier as proof that the attestation key is authentic. It is deliberately not required to be any particular format (such as an X.509 certificate).

Additional signing keys may be provisioned explicitly instead of relying on the automatically generated default key by using the io.systemd.Report.TPM2SignerKeyManager Varlink interface, registered as an AF_UNIX socket at /run/systemd/io.systemd.Report.TPM2SignerKeyManager. The interface can be queried with varlinkctl introspect /run/systemd/io.systemd.Report.TPM2SignerKeyManager.
If more than one key is present, a signed report is generated with each of them.
